doc.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
doc.interviewee: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams

chapter: Funerals, societies and the future of fiddling
title: Everyone's names recorded for the tape; young people prefer new music
summary: The interviewer gets names from all present for the record, including Robert Pete Williams and Dick Allen, and notes nobody else plays old-time fiddle locally; Cage says youngsters do not play his kind.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Not many of them. They may find them going to school. It's pretty good sometimes. But they can't play that real dance music, huh? Not those old-time numbers. I haven't heard... Oh, but they play something else. They play something else. They like the new music now. Yeah. I never do hear any of them. You know, I used to hear... When I grew up in Georgia, out in the country, I used to hear plenty of fiddle players and banjo pickers. Well, nobody played that up here with... He's the only one. ...and he's fast with you. Yeah. He's the only one I ever know. I've been here 53 years. I ain't never hear nobody play. We ought to get everybody's name down who's here. Yeah. You got new people. Let's see. What's your name? We might as well start with him. We got your name. Pete, you want to tell him? Robert Pete Williams. And can we get your name, Miss Kay? Robert Pete Williams. Robert Pete Williams. Robert Pete Williams. Robert Pete Williams. Robert Pete Williams. And you're... Dick Cook. Alan or Ellen. Say, man, do you want to put your name down? No, you don't give me... I, Hickenbottom. Hickenbottom. Hickenbottom. Hickenbottom. And your first name? I. I. All right. My name is Dick Allen. So we got everybody's name down in case we all talk at once. I don't know who's who. But... You got anything else you want to tell the young students when they come to study music at the university? Me? Yeah. You want to tell them how to play?
No, they don't play my kind.
